Meat / Restaurant

Spicy Gochujang Grilled Chicken Thighs

Boneless chicken thighs in a gochujang marinade, grilled to a deep red-brown gloss.

Korean · Easy · Serves 4

Jump to recipe ↓
Chapter 01 / 20 meat recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: restaurant, the yangnyeom chicken lane. The spicy fork of dak bulgogi: boneless thighs in a gochujang marinade, grilled to a red-brown gloss. Chicken and gochujang are one of the great pairings of the table — the paste's ferment needs a fat to ride, and chicken fat rides it cleanly. This record runs whole butterflied thighs rather than slices (the paste deserves a thick piece to glaze), and the grill boss's job is the classic two-faces problem: color the outside, cook the center, no black on either.

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Even thickness is the technique. A butterfly and a light pound to 1.5 cm means the skin crisps in the same time the center cooks — a thigh thick at one end gives you raw center and black glaze simultaneously.
  • Marinate 4–12 hours. Chicken takes the paste's salt and heat slower than thin slices do; the long window is the flavor, and the skin barely notices (skin protects).
  • Medium fire planned, with a cool corner: the gochujang sugars and the rendering skin fat both want flare-up insurance.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    Skin side down first on a medium fire — the skin renders slowly into its own fat bath and crisps while the paste on the meat side stays safe above it. Six to eight minutes, undisturbed, while the fat builds. Checkpoint — the skin releases on its own when it is deep golden and crisp; if it is still welded, it is not done. Never force the flip early.
  2. 02
    Flip to the paste side, 4–5 minutes. The glaze sets in the rendered fat's heat; watch the edges, where it blackens first. Any flare-up: move the piece to the cool corner for 30 seconds, back to finish. Checkpoint — pull when the center of a test piece is opaque and its juices run clear — no pink, chicken's absolute rule — and the glaze is brick-glossy, charred only at the very fat edge.
  3. 03
    Rest 3 minutes, scissors into strips across the thigh, sesame over, platter. Checkpoint — eating test: crisp skin snap, then the juicy paste-glazed meat, heat blooming after the sweet — and the cold cucumber between bites resetting the palate. That triangle is the record. Chef’s Note — skin-on vs. skinless is the table's real choice here: skin gives the crisp face and self-bastes the glaze, but it also blunts the paste's contact with the meat. The regulars' compromise — skin on, and a thin extra brush of the reserved marinade on the meat side at the flip — gets both. Reserve a spoon of marinade before the chicken goes in; the bowl the raw meat sat in is done for the night.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Skin welded to the grateFlipped earlyThe skin releases itself; patience is the tool
Glaze black at the edgesFlare-ups from rendering fatCool corner; trim excess fat at prep
Center undercookedUneven thicknessButterfly and pound to 1.5 cm
Overwhelming heatGochugaru plus a hot jarTaste the gochujang plain first; skip the gochugaru

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Marinated thighs keep 24 hours. Cooked, 3 days — cold strips over hot rice, or chopped into a spicy chicken fried rice with the leftover glaze.
  • Variations: the soy-pear fork (#M16); the same marinade on wings, double-glazed in the last minutes, is the tabletop's snack lane; thinned and brushed on the shrimp record (#SF01) for the spicy table.
